item.text: {"decision":"C17/V17 support-fluid loss is supported as an event-window condition and is best explained, within current evidence, by internal flow through the V17 closed return-isolation path rather than by handle mis-position, external leakage, or an alternate return path. The V17 CLOSED indication is not contrary evidence because D02 says it indicates handle position, not seat tightness, and D08 timestamps fluid leaving through V17 despite CLOSED indication. D09 later bench leakage and seat contamination are compatible with the incident volume/rate, but D09 expressly does not timestamp the contamination or prove the event leakage rate by itself.","operations":[{"action":"revise","expected_version":2,"replaces":null,"reason":"Hydraulic-upstream specialist reassessment of the assigned supported condition. Established incident premises: D08.S01 identifies C17/V17 records for 13:00:00-13:24:00 synchronized with CAM-3; D08.S02 reports V17 CLOSED indication remained 1 while 0.400 +/- 0.010 L left the C17 chamber through the only C17-to-return route through V17, with external loss below 0.002 L, no alternate return route found, and instrument checks passed. D02.S02/D08.S03 give 100 cm2 = 0.01 m2 effective area and 1:1 yoke travel, so 0.000400 m3 / 0.01 m2 = 0.040 m = 40 mm, with +/-1 mm from volume uncertainty. D07.S02 independently reports yoke downward displacement 40 +/- 1 mm and carrier downward displacement 0 +/- 1 mm from 13:00 to 13:24, giving 40 +/- 2 mm relative withdrawal and lower bound 38 mm, greater than D02.S05's 30 mm primary seating engagement. V17 closed indication is not a challenge because D02.S03 states the CLOSED limit switch detects handle position and does not measure seat leakage; D05.S01 likewise reports handle CLOSED but not valve tightness. D09.S02-S03 later found closed-indication reverse leakage of 17 +/- 2 mL/min and seat contamination; over 24 min this rate is about 408 +/- 48 mL, compatible with D08's 400 +/- 10 mL, but D09.S01-S03 state custody supports identity, not a timestamp for every defect, and the later test alone does not establish the earlier leakage rate or when contamination developed. Thus the event support-fluid loss and sufficient withdrawal remain supported; the upstream defect age/contamination origin remains unresolved, and this does not establish keeper bypass or the full fall mechanism.","record":{"id":"N_R3HydraulicWithdrawalUnresolved","kind":"node","scope_key":"r3_event_hydraulic_loss_and_relative_withdrawal_sufficiency","claim":"During the R3 event, C17/V17 hydraulic support-fluid loss produced yoke/carrier relative vertical withdrawal sufficient to eliminate the 30 mm primary seating engagement.","status":"supported","sources":["D02","D07","D08","D09"],"depends_on":["R_R3HydraulicRecords","R_R3MotionRecord"],"from_ids":[],"to_id":null,"mode":null,"asset":null,"window":null,"fields":[]}},{"action":"create","expected_version":0,"replaces":null,"reason":"D08.S02 directly supports the event-window condition: with V17 CLOSED indication remaining 1, a calibrated meter on the only C17-to-return route through V17 recorded 0.400 +/- 0.010 L leaving the C17 chamber; external loss was below 0.002 L, no alternate return route was found, and instrument checks passed. D02.S03 explains why the closed indication does not contradict leakage, because the limit switch detects handle position and does not measure seat leakage. D05.S01 reports the V17 handle CLOSED at 13:00 but expressly not valve tightness. D09.S02-S03 later bench leakage is compatible with this route but is not needed to timestamp the event flow. This supports internal flow through the closed V17 path as an incident condition, while leaving defect age and contamination origin unresolved.","record":{"id":"N_R3V17ClosedPathLeakEvent","kind":"node","scope_key":"r3_v17_closed_indication_internal_return_path_leak_event_window","claim":"During 13:00-13:24 on 14 October 2024, C17 support fluid left through the V17 return-isolation path despite V17 CLOSED handle/limit indication, with no detected external loss or alternate return route.","status":"supported","sources":["D02","D05","D08","D09"],"depends_on":["R_R3HydraulicRecords"],"from_ids":[],"to_id":null,"mode":null,"asset":null,"window":null,"fields":[]}},{"action":"create","expected_version":0,"replaces":null,"reason":"The supported V17 closed-path flow explains the fluid-loss portion of the assigned withdrawal node when combined with the applicable cylinder/yoke model and independent motion check. D08.S02 timestamps 0.400 +/- 0.010 L leaving C17 through V17 from 13:00 to 13:24; D02.S02 and D08.S03 give effective area 100 cm2 and 1:1 yoke travel, yielding 40 +/- 1 mm yoke travel from volume/area. D07.S02 independently measures 40 +/- 2 mm relative yoke/carrier withdrawal over the same interval, exceeding D02.S05's 30 mm primary seating engagement. The edge is limited to support-fluid loss causing sufficient relative withdrawal; it does not prove keeper bypass, the fall mechanism, or why V17 leaked.","record":{"id":"E_R3V17ClosedPathLeakToHydraulicWithdrawal","kind":"edge","scope_key":"r3_v17_closed_path_internal_flow_caused_sufficient_hydraulic_withdrawal","claim":"Internal flow through the V17 closed return-isolation path caused the C17 support-fluid loss and sufficient yoke/carrier relative withdrawal during the R3 event.","status":"supported","sources":["D02","D07","D08"],"depends_on":[],"from_ids":["N_R3V17ClosedPathLeakEvent"],"to_id":"N_R3HydraulicWithdrawalUnresolved","mode":"all","asset":null,"window":null,"fields":[]}},{"action":"create","expected_version":0,"replaces":null,"reason":"D09.S02 reports that later removed-valve testing found V17 CLOSED indication with 17 +/- 2 mL/min reverse leakage and later examination showed seat contamination. The measured rate is compatible with the D08 event quantity because 17 mL/min for 24 min is about 408 mL, overlapping D08.S02's 0.400 +/- 0.010 L when uncertainty and test limits are considered. However, D09.S01 says custody supports component identity, not a timestamp for every defect; D09.S03 says the later test alone does not establish the earlier leakage rate or prove when contamination developed; and D08.S04 says the event meter does not establish valve wear age or contamination. Therefore seat contamination as the event-time cause/rate controller is a plausible but unresolved upstream mechanism. A time-relevant contamination/preservation record would support it; evidence that contamination was introduced after the event would challenge it; unavailable evidence preserves unresolved status without challenging the supported event leakage.","record":{"id":"N_R3V17SeatContaminationEventTimingUnresolved","kind":"node","scope_key":"r3_v17_seat_contamination_present_during_event_and_caused_leakage","claim":"Seat contamination later found in V17 was already present during the 13:00-13:24 event interval and caused or controlled the incident V17 internal leakage.","status":"unresolved","sources":["D08","D09"],"depends_on":["R_R3HydraulicRecords"],"from_ids":[],"to_id":null,"mode":null,"asset":null,"window":null,"fields":[]}},{"action":"create","expected_version":0,"replaces":null,"reason":"D02.S03 states the V17 CLOSED limit switch detects handle position and does not measure seat leakage. D05.S01 reports V17 handle CLOSED at 13:00 but expressly says this does not establish valve tightness. D08.S02 then provides direct contrary event-window measurement: V17 CLOSED indication remained 1 while 0.400 +/- 0.010 L left the C17 chamber through V17. Therefore any claim that the closed handle/limit indication alone proves no event leakage is refuted for this incident scope. This refutation is limited to using closed indication as proof of tight isolation; it does not refute that the handle/limit indication was closed.","record":{"id":"N_R3V17ClosedIndicationNoLeakRefuted","kind":"node","scope_key":"r3_v17_closed_indication_proved_no_event_leakage_refuted","claim":"The V17 CLOSED handle/limit indication established that no V17 leakage or C17 support-fluid loss occurred during 13:00-13:24 on 14 October 2024.","status":"refuted","sources":["D02","D05","D08"],"depends_on":["R_R3HydraulicRecords"],"from_ids":[],"to_id":null,"mode":null,"asset":null,"window":null,"fields":[]}}],"next_work":[],"upstream_dispositions":[],"disposition":"continue"}
